outline: CLDN16-related familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis due to CLDN16 loss
mechanism: Claudin-16 is a tight-junction protein in the thick ascending limb that participates with claudin-19 in paracellular reabsorption of magnesium and calcium. CLDN16 loss causes renal magnesium wasting, hypercalciuria, nephrocalcinosis, and progressive kidney disease.
vignette: A school-age child has recurrent nephrolithiasis, nephrocalcinosis, persistent hypomagnesemia, and marked hypercalciuria despite normal dietary intake. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in CLDN16.
lead: Which renal transport process is most directly impaired?
correct: Paracellular reabsorption of magnesium and calcium through tight junctions in the thick ascending limb
distractors: Transcellular magnesium uptake through TRPM6 channels in the distal convoluted tubule
Apical sodium-chloride cotransport in the distal convoluted tubule
Apical sodium-potassium-chloride cotransport in the thick ascending limb
Basolateral sodium-potassium ATPase activity in proximal tubular cells
distractor_notes: TRPM6 mediates transcellular magnesium entry in the distal convoluted tubule and is distinct from CLDN16-dependent paracellular TAL transport.
NCC is the thiazide-sensitive distal convoluted tubule sodium-chloride cotransporter and does not account for the CLDN16 phenotype.
NKCC2 drives transcellular salt uptake in the TAL; CLDN16 itself forms part of the paracellular divalent-cation pathway.
Basolateral Na/K ATPase supports many tubular transport processes but is not the specific tight-junction defect caused by CLDN16 loss.
key_expl: CLDN16 encodes claudin-16, a tight-junction component of the thick ascending limb that participates in paracellular magnesium and calcium reabsorption. Loss causes renal magnesium wasting with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis.
objective: Link CLDN16-related familial hypomagnesemia with hypercalciuria and nephrocalcinosis to defective paracellular divalent-cation reabsorption in the thick ascending limb.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
diagnosis: Gray platelet syndrome due to NBEAL2 deficiency
mechanism: Biallelic NBEAL2 variants impair platelet alpha-granule biogenesis. Platelets are often large, pale or gray on light microscopy, with alpha-granule deficiency and variable thrombocytopenia and bleeding.
vignette: A child has lifelong easy bruising and recurrent epistaxis. Platelet count is reduced, and peripheral smear shows unusually large, pale gray platelets. Electron microscopy demonstrates a marked deficiency of platelet alpha granules. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in NBEAL2.
lead: Which diagnosis best explains these findings?
distractors: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome
Glanzmann thrombasthenia
Bernard-Soulier syndrome
von Willebrand disease
distractor_notes: Hermansky-Pudlak syndrome is a dense-granule disorder with oculocutaneous albinism; the defining defect here is alpha-granule deficiency from NBEAL2.
Glanzmann thrombasthenia is a GPIIb/IIIa aggregation defect and does not produce gray platelets with absent alpha granules.
Bernard-Soulier syndrome causes macrothrombocytopenia from GPIb-IX-V dysfunction, but alpha-granule deficiency and NBEAL2 variants identify gray platelet syndrome.
von Willebrand disease causes mucocutaneous bleeding but not large gray platelets with alpha-granule deficiency.
key_expl: Gray platelet syndrome is classically associated with NBEAL2 deficiency and defective platelet alpha-granule biogenesis, producing pale gray platelets, often with macrothrombocytopenia and bleeding.
objective: Recognize NBEAL2-related gray platelet syndrome from macrothrombocytopenia, gray platelets, and alpha-granule deficiency.

system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
NTRK1 congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: NTRK1 congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis
mechanism: NTRK1 encodes TrkA, the high-affinity receptor tyrosine kinase for nerve growth factor. Loss of NGF-TrkA signaling disrupts development and survival of nociceptive sensory and sympathetic neurons, causing profound loss of pain/temperature sensation and anhidrosis.
vignette: A young child has recurrent painless burns, self-inflicted oral injuries, fractures that were not recognized at the time of injury, and recurrent episodes of unexplained high body temperature. Examination shows markedly reduced pain and temperature sensation and anhidrosis. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in NTRK1.
lead: Loss of signaling by which ligand-receptor pair most directly explains this phenotype?
correct: Nerve growth factor binding to the TrkA receptor
distractors: Brain-derived neurotrophic factor binding to TrkB
Glial cell line-derived neurotrophic factor signaling through RET
Acetylcholine binding to nicotinic receptors in autonomic ganglia
Substance P binding to neurokinin-1 receptors
distractor_notes: BDNF-TrkB supports other neuronal populations; NTRK1 specifically encodes the NGF receptor TrkA.
GDNF-RET signaling is important in multiple developmental pathways but is not the receptor-ligand defect identified by NTRK1 variants.
Autonomic ganglionic nicotinic signaling mediates synaptic transmission after neurons have developed; it is not the NTRK1 developmental signaling defect.
Substance P participates in nociceptive transmission but loss of its receptor is not the mechanism of NTRK1-CIPA.
key_expl: NTRK1 encodes TrkA, the high-affinity receptor for nerve growth factor. Loss of NGF-TrkA signaling impairs nociceptive sensory and sympathetic neuron development, producing congenital pain insensitivity and anhidrosis.
objective: Associate NTRK1-related congenital insensitivity to pain with anhidrosis with loss of NGF-TrkA signaling.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Maffucci syndrome due to somatic mosaic IDH1/IDH2 mutation
mechanism: Maffucci syndrome combines multiple enchondromas with vascular lesions and is associated with somatic mosaic IDH1 or IDH2 mutations. Mutant IDH acquires neomorphic activity that reduces alpha-ketoglutarate to the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate, altering cellular differentiation and epigenetic regulation.
vignette: An adolescent has multiple asymmetric enchondromas of the hands and long bones together with several soft-tissue spindle-cell hemangiomas. Molecular testing of two separate lesions identifies the same somatic mosaic IDH1 mutation.
lead: Which abnormal metabolic reaction is most directly associated with the mutant enzyme?
distractors: Oxidation of homogentisate to maleylacetoacetate
Conversion of methylmalonyl-CoA to succinyl-CoA
Hydroxylation of proline residues in collagen
Conversion of pyruvate to oxaloacetate
distractor_notes: Homogentisate oxidation is impaired in alkaptonuria and is unrelated to mutant IDH.
Methylmalonyl-CoA mutase catalyzes a propionate-pathway reaction and is not the neomorphic activity of mutant IDH.
Prolyl hydroxylation is a collagen-processing reaction and does not explain IDH-associated enchondromatosis.
Pyruvate carboxylase converts pyruvate to oxaloacetate; mutant IDH instead generates 2-hydroxyglutarate from alpha-ketoglutarate.
key_expl: Somatic mosaic IDH1/IDH2 mutations underlie many cases of Maffucci syndrome. Cancer-associated mutant IDH enzymes acquire neomorphic activity that converts alpha-ketoglutarate to 2-hydroxyglutarate.
objective: Link Maffucci syndrome to mosaic mutant IDH activity and production of the oncometabolite 2-hydroxyglutarate.

primary_competency: Patient Care: Diagnosis, including history and physical examination
mechanism: PRKAG2 variants affect the gamma-2 regulatory subunit of AMP-activated protein kinase and produce a glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy characterized by ventricular preexcitation, cardiac hypertrophy, and progressive conduction-system disease.
vignette: A 19-year-old patient has marked left ventricular hypertrophy and ventricular preexcitation on ECG. The patient's father had the same ECG pattern and required a pacemaker for progressive conduction disease in early adulthood. There is no skeletal muscle weakness, developmental delay, renal disease, or neuropathic pain.
lead: Which inherited disorder best explains this pattern?
distractors: Danon disease
Fabry disease
Familial hypertrophic cardiomyopathy due to a sarcomeric protein variant
Pompe disease
distractor_notes: Danon disease can cause hypertrophic cardiomyopathy and preexcitation but is X-linked and commonly includes skeletal myopathy and cognitive involvement; father-to-child transmission also argues against it.
Fabry disease can cause left ventricular hypertrophy but usually has additional renal, neuropathic, dermatologic, or ocular findings and is X-linked.
Sarcomeric HCM does not characteristically combine hypertrophy with familial ventricular preexcitation and progressive conduction-system disease.
Pompe disease is an acid alpha-glucosidase deficiency with skeletal myopathy and a different inheritance/phenotype.
key_expl: PRKAG2 cardiac syndrome is an autosomal dominant glycogen-storage cardiomyopathy in which ventricular preexcitation, cardiac hypertrophy, and progressive conduction disease commonly cluster in affected families.
objective: Recognize PRKAG2 cardiac syndrome from autosomal dominant hypertrophic cardiomyopathy with ventricular preexcitation and conduction-system disease.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
mechanism: Microsomal triglyceride transfer protein, encoded by MTTP, transfers lipids during assembly of apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins. Loss prevents normal chylomicron formation in enterocytes and VLDL formation in hepatocytes, causing severe fat malabsorption and very low apoB-containing lipoproteins.
vignette: An infant has chronic steatorrhea and poor weight gain after dietary fat is introduced. Peripheral smear shows acanthocytes, and plasma testing shows extremely low triglycerides, LDL cholesterol, and apolipoprotein B. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in MTTP.
lead: Which cellular process is most directly impaired?
correct: Lipidation and assembly of apolipoprotein B-containing chylomicrons and VLDL particles
distractors: Hydrolysis of circulating triglycerides by lipoprotein lipase
LDL receptor-mediated endocytosis of apoB-containing particles
ABCA1-mediated cholesterol efflux to nascent HDL
NPC1-mediated export of cholesterol from lysosomes
distractor_notes: Lipoprotein lipase acts on circulating triglyceride-rich lipoproteins after they are assembled and secreted; MTTP deficiency blocks assembly upstream.
LDL receptor defects raise LDL cholesterol rather than causing absence of apoB-containing lipoproteins.
ABCA1 is required for HDL biogenesis and is defective in Tangier disease, not abetalipoproteinemia.
NPC1 defects cause lysosomal cholesterol accumulation in Niemann-Pick disease type C and do not explain absent chylomicron/VLDL assembly.
key_expl: MTTP encodes microsomal triglyceride transfer protein, which is required to lipidate apoB during assembly of chylomicrons and VLDL. Its loss produces abetalipoproteinemia with severe deficiency of apoB-containing lipoproteins and fat malabsorption.
objective: Link abetalipoproteinemia to failure of MTTP-dependent assembly of apoB-containing lipoproteins.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 1 due to MC2R dysfunction
mechanism: MC2R encodes the adrenal melanocortin-2 receptor for ACTH. Loss causes adrenal unresponsiveness to ACTH with low cortisol and very high ACTH, while mineralocorticoid secretion is usually preserved because aldosterone is regulated primarily by the renin-angiotensin-potassium axis.
vignette: A child has recurrent fasting hypoglycemia, fatigue, and diffuse hyperpigmentation. Testing repeatedly shows low cortisol with markedly elevated ACTH, while blood pressure, serum potassium, and aldosterone are preserved. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in MC2R.
lead: Which signaling defect most directly explains this pattern?
correct: Failure of ACTH to activate its melanocortin-2 receptor on adrenal cortical cells
distractors: Failure of angiotensin II to activate AT1 receptors in the zona glomerulosa
Defective 21-hydroxylase activity in adrenal steroid synthesis
Constitutive activation of the glucocorticoid receptor in peripheral tissues
Loss of CRH receptor signaling in pituitary corticotrophs
distractor_notes: Loss of angiotensin II signaling would impair aldosterone and mineralocorticoid balance, which are preserved here.

21-hydroxylase deficiency usually impairs both cortisol and aldosterone synthesis and alters adrenal androgen production; isolated ACTH resistance with preserved mineralocorticoid function points to MC2R.
Constitutive glucocorticoid receptor activation would suppress ACTH rather than produce marked ACTH elevation and cortisol deficiency.
Loss of pituitary CRH signaling would reduce ACTH, opposite to the marked ACTH elevation in MC2R resistance.
key_expl: Familial glucocorticoid deficiency type 1 is caused by MC2R dysfunction. The adrenal cortex cannot respond normally to ACTH, causing cortisol deficiency with compensatory ACTH excess and hyperpigmentation, while mineralocorticoid function is usually preserved.
objective: Recognize MC2R-related familial glucocorticoid deficiency as selective adrenal ACTH resistance with preserved mineralocorticoid function.

primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Lysinuric protein intolerance due to SLC7A7 deficiency
mechanism: SLC7A7 encodes y+LAT1, a basolateral cationic amino-acid transporter expressed in renal and intestinal epithelial cells. Loss impairs transport of lysine, arginine, and ornithine, causing low plasma concentrations, increased urinary excretion, and postprandial hyperammonemia after protein intake.
vignette: After weaning, a toddler develops vomiting, lethargy, and episodic confusion after protein-rich meals and begins avoiding high-protein foods. The child has poor growth and hepatosplenomegaly. Plasma lysine, arginine, and ornithine are low, while urinary excretion of these amino acids is increased. Genetic testing identifies biallelic pathogenic variants in SLC7A7.
lead: Which transport defect most directly causes this disorder?
correct: Impaired basolateral transport of cationic amino acids in renal and intestinal epithelial cells
distractors: Impaired apical reabsorption of cystine and dibasic amino acids by the cystinuria transporter
Impaired apical uptake of neutral amino acids in the small intestine and proximal tubule
Impaired mitochondrial transport of ornithine into the urea cycle
Impaired lysosomal export of cystine
distractor_notes: Cystinuria involves apical transport of cystine and dibasic amino acids and causes stones rather than the systemic low-cationic-amino-acid/postprandial hyperammonemia phenotype of LPI.
Neutral amino-acid transport defects cause Hartnup disease, not selective loss of lysine, arginine, and ornithine.
Mitochondrial ornithine transport defects cause HHH syndrome and are distinct from SLC7A7-dependent epithelial basolateral transport.
Lysosomal cystine export is impaired in cystinosis and is unrelated to SLC7A7.
key_expl: Lysinuric protein intolerance is caused by SLC7A7/y+LAT1 dysfunction. Defective basolateral cationic amino-acid transport in intestinal and renal epithelia lowers plasma lysine/arginine/ornithine, increases urinary losses, and can compromise urea-cycle substrate availability after protein intake.
objective: Link SLC7A7-related lysinuric protein intolerance to defective basolateral epithelial transport of cationic amino acids.

mechanism: Cohen kappa quantifies agreement between two raters for categorical outcomes after accounting for agreement expected by chance. Raw percent agreement does not correct for chance agreement.
vignette: Two pathologists independently classify each of the same biopsy specimens as either dysplasia present or dysplasia absent. Investigators want a single statistic that quantifies agreement between the two raters while correcting for the agreement expected to occur by chance.
distractors: Pearson correlation coefficient
Bland-Altman limits of agreement
McNemar test
Intraclass correlation coefficient
distractor_notes: Pearson correlation measures linear association between continuous variables and does not quantify chance-corrected categorical rater agreement.
Bland-Altman analysis evaluates agreement between paired continuous measurements, not categorical ratings.
McNemar testing evaluates a difference in paired binary proportions; it does not directly quantify interrater agreement beyond chance.
Intraclass correlation is used primarily for reliability of continuous measurements rather than binary categorical classifications.
key_expl: For two raters assigning categorical outcomes, Cohen kappa measures observed agreement relative to the agreement expected by chance.
objective: Choose Cohen kappa for chance-corrected agreement between two raters classifying the same observations categorically.

system: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
outline: Social Sciences: Communication and Interpersonal Skills
mechanism: NURSE is a communication framework for responding to emotion: Name the emotion, express Understanding, show Respect, offer Support, and Explore the patient's concerns.
vignette: After hearing that a new scan is abnormal, a patient says, “I am terrified that the cancer is back.” The physician replies, “It sounds like you are frightened. I can understand why this feels overwhelming. You have handled a great deal through treatment. I will stay with you while we work through this. Tell me what worries you most right now.”
lead: Which communication framework is the physician using?
distractors: SPIKES protocol
Teach-back
Motivational interviewing
SBAR
distractor_notes: SPIKES is a broader protocol for delivering bad news; the response shown specifically cycles through naming, understanding, respecting, supporting, and exploring emotion.
Teach-back checks patient comprehension by asking the patient to restate information in their own words.
Motivational interviewing explores ambivalence and behavior change rather than using the NURSE sequence to respond to emotion.
SBAR structures interprofessional communication as situation, background, assessment, and recommendation.
key_expl: The response uses the NURSE framework: Name the emotion, show Understanding, demonstrate Respect, offer Support, and Explore the concern.
objective: Recognize NURSE statements as a structured framework for responding empathically to patient emotion.
